question: What Speed Limit (R2-1) sign sizes are shown in Table 2B-1 for conventional single-lane, conventional multi-lane, expressway, and freeway applications?
model_answer: Direct Answer: Table 2B-1 (Regulatory Sign and Plaque Sizes) shows the Speed Limit (R2-1) sign at 24 x 30 inches for conventional single-lane roads, 30 x 36 inches for conventional multi-lane roads, 36 x 48 inches for expressways, and 48 x 60 inches for freeways. The table also lists a minimum size of 18 x 24 inches and an oversized size of 30 x 36 inches, with all dimensions shown as width x height in inches. (Note: the text provisions supplied address R2-1 content and placement, not sizes; the size values come from the table shown in the attached page image.) Standards (mandatory): - "The Speed Limit (R2-1) sign (see Figure 2B-3) shall display the limit established by law, ordinance, regulation, or as adopted by the authorized agency based on an engineering study. The speed limits displayed shall be in multiples of 5 mph." (context on the sign's use; sizing itself is tabulated in Table 2B-1) Visual evidence: - [Image 5] shows Table 2B-1 (Sheet 1 of 6) with the Speed Limit (R2-1) row, Section 2B.21, listing 24 x 30 (Single Lane), 30 x 36 (Multi-Lane), 36 x 48 (Expressway), 48 x 60 (Freeway), 18 x 24 (Minimum), and 30 x 36 (Oversized). - [Image 1] shows Figure 2B-3, illustrating the R2-1 Speed Limit sign design and its related plaques (R2-2P, R2-3P, R2-4P, etc.) referenced by the table. Citations: - Section 2B.21 Standard §13 (p.85) - Figure 2B-3 (p.86) - Page 109
gold_answer: 24 x 30, 30 x 36, 36 x 48, and 48 x 60 inches, respectively.
